messages:
Maya: quick check — we added synthetic queries from the search-sim generator into the reranker holdout (cohort B) to boost sample size. seeing a 0.9 pt NDCG drop vs baseline on the new model. thoughts? :thinking_face:
Kevin: do you mean you merged synthetic queries into the same test set, or created a separate cohort?
Maya: merged. original holdout had 6k queries, synthetic added ~18k. aggregated NDCG went down; MRR roughly unchanged.
Anjali: merging synthetic with human queries can change the distribution a lot — length, term overlap, label sparsity. did you stratify by query length or intent?
Maya: no stratification, just concat.
Sarah: what does the synthetic generator do? paraphrases, random insertions, or template-based?
Maya: it's the search-sim model we used in prod for augmenting cold-start. templates + paraphrase sampling. sometimes shorter queries with high lexical overlap.
Kevin: that explains it. reranker currently tuned for human phrasing. synthetic cohort likely has less lexical variance so position distribution shifts. can you dump doc-query token overlap histograms?
Maya: attaching quick dump in thread: `overlap_hist.png` (placeholder). basic stats: median query len human=6 tokens, synth=3; mean overlap human=0.42, synth=0.65.
Anjali: higher overlap -> reranker gets easier positives so NDCG metric can be misleading if label space changed. MRR stable probably because top-1 still similar. We should do per-slice NDCG and PSI between cohorts.
Maya: agreed. I can run per-slice NDCG and bootstrap CIs. any preferred slices?
Kevin: length buckets (1-3,4-6,7+), overlap bins (0-0.3,0.3-0.6,0.6+), and click-intent labels if available. Also track candidate pool size.
Sarah: also check doc truncation/prefixing — synth docs are shorter so not hitting truncation edgecases. could bias token-level model behavior differently after PTQ.
Anjali: good point. if we're planning quantization tests, keep synthetic separated until we know its effect. run an A/B: human-only vs human+synthetic but report metrics separately, not merged.
Maya: running that now. quick note: our eval harness currently normalizes queries by lowercasing and removing punctuation, but generator outputs are already lowercase — might double-normalize.
Kevin: that could reduce signal. show the normalizer snippet?
Maya: `def normalize(q): return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]+", "", q.lower()).strip()` — so double-lowercasing harmless but punctuation removal could be more aggressive than intended.
Anjali: For the bootstrapping, use 1000 resamples and compute 95% CI for delta NDCG and delta MRR. Also compute effect size per-slice and a p-value using permutation test.
Maya: running bootstrap + permutation now. ETA ~20m.
Sarah: if the CI crosses zero for human-only but not for merged, we should avoid merging for release decisions.
Kevin: can we also run a small model-internal diagnostic: feed pairs where only query is synthetic variant vs human and check scoring gap distribution? helps see whether model preference is for lexical cues.
Maya: good call — I'll produce a score-diff histogram.
Anjali: add a small quality gate: if synthetic cohort changes NDCG by >0.5 pts overall OR any length bin shifts >1.0 pt, mark as "synth-impact" and block rollout until investigated.
Maya: noted. creating a ticket in GH: `ml-eval#842` with steps.
Kevin: when you post results, include small reproducible script snippet we can run locally; something like:
```
# sample command
python eval/run_eval.py --holdout human_holdout.json --synthetic synth_holdout.json --slices "len,overlap" --bootstrap 1000
```
Maya: will do. posting results in ~25m.
(eval-bot): CI job `rerank-eval/synth-check` started by Maya — job id 12291.
(eval-bot): job 12291 finished: human-only NDCG=0.712 (95% CI [0.703,0.721]), merged NDCG=0.703 (95% CI [0.698,0.708]), delta=-0.009 (p=0.03).
Maya: initial numbers show a small but statistically significant drop when merging. per-slice: len 1-3 delta -0.02, 4-6 delta -0.004, 7+ delta +0.001. overlap>0.6 delta -0.018.
Anjali: exactly the overlap bin. suggests synthetic too lexically similar. recommendation: keep synth separate for now and refine generator to increase paraphrase diversity, or downweight synth in evaluation sampling.
Sarah: also flag for PTQ runs: run both with and without synth to ensure quantization artifacts aren't conflated with dataset shift.
Maya: filing follow-ups: - keep synth cohort separate in evals - add slice-based gates - update generator sampling temp to increase paraphrase diversity - re-run PTQ smokejobs A/B. I'll attach logs and scripts to GH ticket. :thumbsup:
Kevin: thanks. small pragmatic rule: never change holdout composition mid-experiment without a documented migration plan.
Maya: noted and will add to eval playbook.
(eval-bot): ticket ml-eval#842 created by Maya.
